title: NY State Assembly · District 40
area: Flushing and surrounding neighborhoods in northeastern Queens.

context.text: Incumbent Ron Kim is running unopposed. The Democratic, Republican and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled; Kim advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party lines without appearing on the ballot, and no Republican candidate filed.

summary.text: Ron Kim is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Assembly District 40, first elected in 2012 and the first Korean-American ever elected to the New York State Legislature. He chairs the Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committee and also sits on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Education, Governmental Operations, and Housing committees. He is running unopposed in the 2026 general election.

background.text: Raised in Flushing, Queens from age 7; graduated from Riverdale Country Day School in 1997, earned a B.A. from Hamilton College, and a Master's in Public Administration from Baruch College.

Began his public-service career in then-City Council Member John Liu's office, later worked as an aide to then-Assemblyman Mark Weprin, and held posts at the NYC Department of Buildings and Department of Small Business Services.
Served as a Regional Director for Government and Community Affairs in the administrations of Governors Eliot Spitzer and David Paterson (2007-2010) before his election to the Assembly in 2012.
Chaired the Assembly Task Force on New Americans starting in 2015 and served as Secretary of the Majority Conference starting in 2017.

priorities.text: His official biography describes a career focused on quality education, funding for local schools, and support for small businesses in the Flushing community.

positions.summary: Sponsored A00676, imposing an additional tax on income attributable to long-term capital gains, and A00970, imposing a tax related to executive compensation.
Sponsored A00651, which would require courts to advise noncitizen defendants of deportation risk before a guilty plea and allow withdrawal of a plea if that advisement was not given.

record.text: Chairs the Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committee; also serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions, Education, Governmental Operations, and Housing committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A00676, imposing an additional tax on income attributable to long-term capital gain; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A00970, imposing a tax related to executive compensation; referred to the Ways and Means Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A00651, requiring courts to advise noncitizen defendants of deportation risk before accepting a guilty plea; referred to the Codes Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.
Sponsored A10333, relating to maximum hours for home care aides; referred to the Labor Committee as of February 2026, not enacted as of September 2026.
